arcades.info_text: Typical bowling alley arcade, sadly most of the focus is on redemption games but there are a handful of actual video games to play. It's all quite modern which is actually pretty great, unless of course you're looking for something retro. Most games, bar the Dancing Stage EuroMIX cab, are kept to a really great condition, prices are generally £1 a go, a couple of the bigger machines being £2. / Crowd wise you can often find a lot of kids but they're harmless. Good area for Streetpassing on your Nintendo 3DS! Since Hollywood Bowl is in a leisure park you have a few other attractions such as Odeon, a multitude of places to eat including Nandos, McDonalds, KFC, Pizza Hut, Coast II Coast, Chiquitos, ASK and a couple others I'm forgetting. There is a club nearby called Chicago's which gets very busy on Thursday nights as that is the student night, however I daresay they'd not waste their time in a sub-par arcade over a nightclub haha. / Website says the place is open from 10:00 "til late", I'm not certain what time that means.

arcades.info_text: "As I drove past Merlins to that corner by the Rose and Crown that we all love to see, I noticed the 'Mr B's' arcades had been turned into a 'Jimmy G's' instead. Jimmy Godden has bought both sides of Mr B's, both phase I and II. The larger of the two, phase II, has been completely renovated giving it a more modern look. The roof has been completely torn down and replaced, which must have cost one hell of a lot as I know it to have had an asbestos problem, and could not be touched. I was especially sad to notice the three things phase II offered that no other Leysdown arcade offered had been removed: The Laser quest, 'fun factory' and bumper cars have all been demolished. A new bowling alley has been put in its place however, as well as the bingo being built too. Hope fully with Jimmy owning several other arcades too, he will be able to bring a new lease of life to Leysdown, as I'm sure many people would would agree, it could definitely do with a good renovation. / Jimmy Godden / Jimmy Godden is known as the 'King of the South-Coast', owning various different arcades throughout sea-side towns in the South East of England.
